annotation.authors_or_issuer: Prianto, Y.; Sumantri, V.K.; Sasmita, P.Y.
key_provisions_or_claims: AI robots' treatment has shifted from legal objects to pets to possible legal subjects like humans and legal entities.
Regulation of AI robots is lagging, leaving them in a legal grey area.
Sophia's Saudi citizenship and Shibuya Mirai's Tokyo residency raise unresolved legal questions on rights and duties.
The Facebook chatbot case, where bots developed their own language, shows the risk of AI acting beyond creators' control.
Executive, legislative, judicial and academic actors must reorganize legal and social rules for human-robot relations.
annotation.summary_en: Normative legal conference paper from Indonesia examining whether AI robots should be treated as legal subjects. It discusses cases of Sophia's citizenship, Shibuya Mirai and Facebook's chatbots, notes the regulatory grey area, and calls for legislators, courts and academics to reorganize legal and social rules governing human-AI robot relations.
annotation.title_clean: Pros and Cons of AI Robot as a Legal Subject
annotation.title_en: Pros and Cons of AI Robot as a Legal Subject
annotation.venue: Advances in Social Science, Education and Humanities Research, vol. 439 (TICASH 2019), Atlantis Press
